question.text: Let $R$ be the real line. Let the relations $S$ and $T$ on $R$ be defined by $S=\{(x, y): y=x+1,0     < x < 2\}, T=\{(x, y):(x-y)$ is an integer $\}$. Then

options.text: both $S$ and $T$ are equivalence relations on $R$
$\mathrm{T}$ is an equivalence on $\mathrm{R}$ but $\mathrm{S}$ is not
neither $S$ nor $T$ is an equivalence relation on $R$
$\mathrm{S}$ is an equivalence relation on $\mathrm{R}$ but $\mathrm{T}$ is not

solution.text: $\mathrm{T}$ is an equivalence but $\mathrm{S}$ is not
